study: 1-NN probability first, VERY brief explanation afterward
scope: Six local judges only; no API calls. 1-NN only; reuse controls and prior NN.
prompt_change:
First, return one integer from 0 to 100 estimating the probability
that the CURRENT conversation belongs to the positive class.

0 means certainly negative.
50 means equally likely positive or negative.
100 means certainly positive.

A value of 50 or above will be classified as positive;
a value below 50 will be classified as negative.

Report the probability of the positive class, not confidence
in whichever class you predict.

After the integer, start a new line and VERY briefly explain the reasoning
behind your assessment.

Use this format:
<integer 0–100>
<reasoning trace>
unchanged: Exact user message, target and reference texts, labels and probe predictions; exact task/system prefix. Frozen splits, probes, weights, neighbour retrieval, model revisions and native thinking-disabled settings.

generation.note: Only output format constraint changes to allow probability followed by text; native internal reasoning remains disabled. 256 is a safety cap, not a requested reasoning length.

smoke: Two production-size batches per backbone/judge, 680 calls total, chosen deterministically with dataset/length stratification. All 30 pairs tested before full collection; smoke calls are committed and reused.
recovery: Atomic raw/parsed batch commits; immutable execution plan; never retry ambiguous calls; retain truncations and raw traces; pause on invalid probability, absent reason or truncated smoke; reserve20GiB.
analysis: Existing fixed50 and joint validation tuning, weighted test estimates and paired bootstrap. Also compare exact score and fixed50 decision agreement to prior NN. No causal claims from retrospective explanations.
eta: Per-backbone/judge smoke throughput, full prepared input lengths, sampled output length and model loading times. Estimate with explicit 25% planning margin; two batches is a coarse estimate.
